messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — euc1 (eu-central-1) serving degradation. Multiple 502/504 from edge -> ELB. Error rate spike 00:12 UTC, impact ~20% of requests, some customers reporting timeouts. auto-page: @anna_oncall, @miguel_sre, @oliver_infra. Link: https://metrics.redwood.example/alerts/2167004444 :rotating_light:

anna_oncall: on it. can people paste top graphs? which azs?

miguel_sre: seeing 5xx from proxy layer in euc1a and euc1c. ELB target-group reports lots of Unhealthy. Route53 healthchecks show partial failover to us-east.

oliver_infra: looks like ENI flaps in euc1c right when 5xx bursts happened. kernel conntrack table near full on some NAT instances -> SNAT failures.

lucy_runtime: Confirmed traffic surges causing continuous connection churn. KV cache misses, higher tail latency. CPI traces: backend calls failing with ECONNRESET.

jasmin_support: customer impact: several customers in EU reporting model inference timeouts and 5xx. Support ticket count increased x6. Need clear comms.

anna_oncall: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce DNS TTL for affected records, 2) shift weight away from euc1 Route53 entries to us-east/eur fallback, 3) scale NAT/GW and healthy target registration, 4) roll requests to dedicated capacity where possible. Who can run the Route53 weight change now?

nikhil_network: I can do the DNS weight change. propose: shift 60% away from euc1 to euw1/us-east with 30s TTL. We should also enable cross-zone load balancing on ALBs where disabled.

oliver_infra: scaling NATs now — bump NAT autoscaling group desired from 3 -> 8 in euc1. Starting new NATs (ami-xxxx). Also provisioning extra Az-specific proxy instances.

miguel_sre: running quick health-check script against targets:```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-inference/abcd1234
# then curl edge IPs
for ip in $(cat edges.txt); do curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null http://$ip/health || echo fail:$ip; done
```

lucy_runtime: logs from runtime: ```
[2026-03-15T00:11:23Z] conn_reset backend=instance-45 err=ECONNRESET
[2026-03-15T00:11:24Z] conntrack: table full, drop conn for src=10.0.12.45:34567
```

anna_oncall: good. nikhil, proceed with DNS weight shift and reduce TTL to 30s. post here when done. miguel, keep running target re-registration and health checks. oliver, NATs + AZ proxies - status?

nikhil_network: executing change: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZONE123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc1","Weight":40,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.120.1.12"}]}}]}'``` applying weighted routing for api.redwood.example.

deploy-bot: DNS change submitted (chg id: C123456789). propagation expected ~30s.

miguel_sre: after shifting weights we see 15% drop in 5xx within 90s. still seeing timeouts from clients pinned to euc1.

oliver_infra: NAT ASG scaled to 8 healthy nodes. conntrack freed up. restarting some proxy instances to flush stale connections.
\
anna_oncall: quick commerce: run `conntrack -L | wc -l` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on NATs to check headroom. miguel can you paste outputs?
\
miguel_sre: outputs: ```
# on nat-12
$ conntrack -L | wc -l
327680
$ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 524288
``` headroom but table saturation transient. we cleared many with restart, counts dropping to ~40k.

lucy_runtime: runtime tail latency back to acceptable for majority, but 502s still at ~2%.

jasmin_support: started statuspage incident: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-4721, message drafted: "We are experiencing degraded inference in eu-central-1. We are mitigating traffic and will provide updates."

anna_oncall: accepted. create internal incident ticket and postmortem. tagging SRE, infra, runtime.

miguel_sre: performing targeted deregistration of unhealthy targets in euc1c TG, then re-registering after warmup. Command: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234``` then `register-targets` after checks. Doing canary deregister to avoid cascading.

oliver_infra: observed one EC2 host with repeated ENI detach logs -> aws-side issue? raising support case to AWS for possible network hypervisor instability in euc1c. Case opened: 9876543210.
\
anna_oncall: on-call handoff: @anna_oncall -> @miguel_sre in 40m. Miguel will take lead for overnight. Anna will stay to confirm customer comms.
\
miguel_sre: taking lead. tracking board updated. I'm escalating to infra for cross-zone LB settings and to runtime for any model-level retries.
\
nikhil_network: Route53 weight stayed at 40% euc1, 30% us-east, 30% euw1. TTL 30s. Edge logs show gradual draining of connections from euc1.

lucy_runtime: implemented short-term client-side retry bump for EU clients (2 -> 4 attempts) via config flag on CDN edge, will revert after stabilization.

jasmin_support: customer comms updated: added timestamp and next update ETA +30m.

miguel_sre: metrics now: 5xx down to 0.8%, latency P95 near baseline. still monitoring for residual errors.

oliver_infra: AWS case update: they see network plane anomalies in euc1c affecting ENI attach/detach. They recommended instance reboot for affected hosts as workaround; will coordinate if needed.

anna_oncall: decision: do not reboot more hosts unless necessary. continue DNS weight shift and scaling. keep case open with AWS.

deploy-bot: pager cleared for incident-bot (acknowledged).

miguel_sre: rolling back client retry bump after metrics stable for 5m.

lucy_runtime: runtime asserts pass, no QPS throttles.

jasmin_support: ticket volume returning to baseline, customers updated with resolution message: "Traffic rebalanced away from impacted AZ; service returning to normal. We’ll follow up with postmortem."

anna_oncall: marking incident as mitigated at 00:45 UTC. creating follow-up postmortem doc. Owners: miguel_sre (lead), oliver_infra (infra root cause), lucy_runtime (runtime regressions).

miguel_sre: summary notes for postmortem: root cause likely AWS network/hypervisor anomalies in euc1c causing ENI flaps and transient conntrack saturation on NATs which led to SNAT failures and increased 5xx. Contributing factors: low default conntrack tuning on NATs, some ALBs not cross-zone enabled, DNS TTL too long for rapid failover. Action items: 1) increase conntrack headroom and monitoring; 2) enable cross-zone LB where safe; 3) lower TTL for critical records to 30s during maintenance windows; 4) add runbook steps for weighted Route53 emergency shift; 5) automate NAT autoscaling faster.

anna_oncall: assigning action items in tracker. will schedule postmortem review tomorrow 09:00 UTC. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
